articles.title: Cyclone Akvan Begins Landfall Near Gopalpur; Over 3 Lakh Evacuated in Odisha
articles.excerpt: The storm crossed the coast near Gopalpur at 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph on Friday morning after weakening from a severe cyclonic storm, with 423 rescue teams deployed, dozens of trains cancelled and a red alert in two north Andhra districts.
articles.image_caption: Satellite image of Cyclone Akvan over the Bay of Bengal on November 18, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora readers with family along the Odisha and north Andhra coast get the landfall timing, evacuation scale, train cancellations and closure dates in one place.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Heat-Linked Gene Variant Helps Male Malaria Mosquitoes Mate, May Aid Transmission
articles.excerpt: A Cell study of Anopheles stephensi, the urban malaria vector native to South Asia, finds a deletion in the timeless clock gene gives males a mating edge in high heat while leaving females easier for the malaria parasite to infect.
articles.image_caption: Blood-feeding female Anopheles stephensi mosquitoes. The species, native to South Asia, is the subject of a Cell study linking a timeless-gene variant to heat adaptation and malaria transmission.
articles.nri_angle: Anopheles stephensi is the urban malaria mosquito native to India and South Asia, so a heat adaptation that could raise transmission matters for Indian cities and for diaspora families who travel into its range.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: Over 80,000 Evacuated in Odisha as Landfall Nears Friday Noon
articles.excerpt: Evacuations have risen past 80,000 against a 2-lakh target, 74 rescue teams are deployed, and the IMD now fixes Akvan's landfall between Narsapur and Puri, close to east of Gopalpur, by noon on Friday, November 20.
articles.image_caption: Waves pound a shoreline under grey skies as people watch from the beach, with Cyclone Akvan approaching the Odisha-Andhra coast. Odisha has evacuated more than 80,000 people ahead of the expected landfall on Friday, November 20.
articles.nri_angle: Readers with family in coastal Odisha and north Andhra Pradesh face a Friday-noon landfall, with trains and a Chennai–Yangon flight already cancelled or rescheduled.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Signs ₹1,976 Crore Deal With Israel's IAI to Upgrade Navy's Barak Missiles
articles.excerpt: The contract upgrades seven Barak-1 point defence systems — launchers, radars and command systems bought in 2000 — with new hardware and software, with BEL and BDL as IAI's industry partners in India.
articles.image_caption: Officials pose with the signed contract documents in New Delhi after the Ministry of Defence signed the Barak upgrade contract with Israel Aerospace Industries. The ₹1,976.40 crore deal covers hardware and software upgrades to seven Barak-1 point defence systems on Indian Navy warships.
articles.nri_angle: The upgrade keeps a 25-year-old Israeli-supplied shield on India's frontline warships while the indigenous VL-SRSAM replacement is developed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

Defence Acquisition Council approved the upgrade
Contract signed for Barak-1 upgrade

articles.title: Tanker With Three Indians Hit Near Hormuz; Accounts Differ on Crew Casualties
articles.excerpt: India's shipping minister says all three Indian seafarers and the whole crew of the MT Navig8 Messi are safe; the operator reports one crew member missing and 11 injured.
articles.nri_angle: Indian seafarers crew a large share of the world's merchant fleet; three Indians were aboard the Navig8 Messi, and one Indian from the Tara Gas attack two days earlier is still missing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: MT Tara Gas attacked, one Indian seafarer missing.
MT Navig8 Messi attacked, conflicting reports emerge.
India's minister confirms all crew safe.

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan Veers North and Weakens; Landfall Window Now Narsapur to Puri
articles.excerpt: The IMD's revised forecast moves the November 20 landfall zone into Odisha's reach, cuts the expected intensity to a severe cyclonic storm, and puts 10 Andhra Pradesh districts on rain alert.
articles.image_caption: A satellite image shows Cyclone Akvan over the Bay of Bengal, east of India's coast.
articles.nri_angle: Families in the US and Gulf with relatives in coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha should note the landfall point is still uncertain; IMD updates on Wednesday night are the next reliable marker.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bombay High Court Quashes ICICI Bank's Sanction to Prosecute Chanda Kochhar
articles.excerpt: Justice Milind Jadhav held that the RBI, not ICICI Bank's board, is the competent authority to sanction prosecution of a bank's head under the Prevention of Corruption Act, and that the bank failed to apply its mind.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay High Court building in Mumbai, seen from across the Oval Maidan.
articles.nri_angle: The ruling is a closely watched governance test for India's largest private-sector banks, whose shares are widely held by NRI and foreign institutional investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Naidu Seeks Immediate Central Aid as Two Cyclones Leave Losses Above ₹7,000 Crore
articles.excerpt: The Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister briefed Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in Delhi on Tuesday, with preliminary estimates putting combined damage from Cyclones Arnav and Murasu above ₹7,000 crore.
articles.image_caption: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu review documents at their meeting in New Delhi. Naidu sought immediate Central assistance after Cyclones Arnav and Murasu caused losses the state preliminarily estimates at more than Rs 7,000 crore.
articles.nri_angle: Andhra Pradesh families in the diaspora are watching both the relief decision and a third approaching cyclone, Akvan, due to make landfall on November 20.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Central assessment team completes field inspections in four Andhra districts; state puts Murasu damage at ₹2,484.43 crore
Naidu meets Finance Minister Sitharaman in New Delhi and seeks immediate Central assistance
Cyclone Akvan forecast to make landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast

articles.title: US Loses Measles Elimination Status After 26 Years as Cases Pass 5,400
articles.excerpt: PAHO ruled on November 17 that measles has circulated uninterrupted in the United States for more than a year. Mexico and Bolivia lost their status in the same announcement.
articles.image_caption: A Pennsylvania Department of Health flyer advertises a measles vaccination clinic held on November 4, 2026. Pennsylvania has reported the most measles cases of any state this year, as the United States lost its measles elimination status.
articles.nri_angle: With measles endemic again in the US, Indian families there — and relatives visiting from India — should check MMR records, especially for infants and school-age children.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Music Economy Generated Rs 17,401 Crore in Gross Value in 2025, EY Finds
articles.excerpt: The EY-IPRS report puts economy-wide music value up 45% since 2023, with independent music at 43% of digital consumption — while direct recording and publishing revenue was Rs 5,433 crore and only 55% of surveyed authors earn full-time from music.
articles.nri_angle: Indian music's growth is increasingly driven by independent regional artists and streaming, the same catalogue diaspora listeners consume abroad; 19% of streams of Indian music on the platforms IPRS tracked were generated outside India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two Killed, Including a Three-Year-Old, as Delhi House Collapses in Jwala Nagar
articles.excerpt: Six tenants were pulled from the Vivek Vihar building in Shahdara and taken to Hedgewar Hospital; officials say the first-floor slab and girder gave way, and the cause is still under investigation.
articles.nri_angle: Building collapses in ageing, densely rented housing are a recurring safety concern in Delhi that diaspora families with relatives in such homes follow closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: At Least 8 Killed as Bus Plunges Into 100-Metre Gorge in Tehri Garhwal
articles.excerpt: The Haridwar-Chamoli bus lost control near Gular Bazar at about 4:30 a.m. on Tuesday and fell below the bridge on the Rishikesh-Badrinath highway; 26 injured passengers were pulled out as the rescue continued.
articles.image_caption: The wrecked bus lies in a stream at the bottom of the gorge near Gular Bazar in Tehri Garhwal, with police and rescue personnel at the scene. The Haridwar to Chamoli bus fell nearly 100 metres from the Rishikesh-Badrinath highway early on Tuesday, killing at least eight people.
articles.nri_angle: The crash was on the Rishikesh-Badrinath highway, the Char Dham pilgrim route also used by NRI families visiting Uttarakhand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Born in Mozambique, Raised in Rajkot: Dolly Vadalia Gets Indian Passport After 26 Years
articles.excerpt: A missed consular birth registration left her without citizenship proof despite a lifetime in India. A Home Ministry memorandum, after MP intervention and verification in Mozambique, has ended the case.
articles.nri_angle: The case is a direct caution for Indian parents abroad: a child born overseas needs consular birth registration within one year to secure citizenship by descent, or the child can face decades without a passport.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two Old Antibiotics Together Reverse Isoniazid Resistance in Drug-Resistant TB, IISc Study Finds
articles.excerpt: Pairing isoniazid with vancomycin restored the frontline drug's power against resistant strains in patient-derived samples and mice — laboratory evidence the authors say now warrants a clinical trial.
articles.nri_angle: India carries 25% of the world's TB cases; a resistance-reversing pairing of two existing drugs is directly relevant to Indian families and to diaspora readers following Indian public-health research.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: INDIA Bloc Seeks Supreme Court Nod to Put 48 Questions to Election Commission
articles.excerpt: Opposition leaders want sworn, record-backed answers on whether the SIR decisions and the Commission's own affidavit were really approved unanimously.
articles.nri_angle: The SIR decides who stays on India's voter rolls, including electors who live abroad part of the year, and the case tests how the poll body's biggest decisions are recorded.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Heads to Manila for ASEAN-India and East Asia Summits
articles.excerpt: Maritime cooperation and the $122 billion trade relationship lead the agenda on November 17, with an AITIGA review push — and no confirmed Quad or Trump meeting, the MEA says.
articles.image_caption: File photograph: Prime Minister Narendra Modi speaking at an event.
articles.nri_angle: Modi said he looks forward to meeting the Indian community in the Philippines during the visit, and the trade and maritime agenda shapes India's engagement across Southeast Asia, home to a large Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Modi arrives in Manila; dinner hosted by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr

articles.title: India's Government Health Spending Triples to Rs 4.14 Lakh Crore, Household Share Falls to 42.7%
articles.excerpt: National Health Accounts 2023-24 show government expenditure up threefold since 2013-14 and out-of-pocket spending down 21.5 percentage points as a share of the total — though per-person household payments still rose.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora readers who fund parents' medical care in India are directly affected by how much of India's health spending households still pay out of pocket.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: China Upgrades VT-4 Tank Used by Pakistan With Anti-Drone Gun, Stronger Armour
articles.excerpt: The upgraded export tank, believed to be designated the VT-4B, adds a 30mm remote weapon station aimed at FPV drones and an active protection system, and is set for display at the Zhuhai airshow next month, the SCMP reported.
articles.image_caption: A VT-4 main battle tank, the Chinese-built export tank operated by the Pakistan Army. China has developed an upgraded variant, believed to be designated the VT-4B, with a 30mm anti-drone weapon station and stronger armour.
articles.nri_angle: The upgrade deepens the China-Pakistan defence axis that shapes India's western-border planning - the backdrop diaspora readers track in India-Pakistan security coverage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Votes Against UN Moratorium on Death Penalty, Citing Sovereign Right to Set Penalties
articles.excerpt: The UNGA Third Committee adopted the Mexico-introduced draft 133-33, but India argued there is no international consensus against capital punishment and that Article 6 of the ICCPR permits it with restrictions.
articles.nri_angle: The vote places India alongside the US, China and Japan in opposing a global executions pause, a position India has held at the UN since 2016.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.card_title: Voting Breakdown on Death Penalty Moratorium

articles.title: Delhi Police Arrest Two Shooters, Foil Planned Attack on Bollywood Actor
articles.excerpt: The Special Cell says Vikas Thakur and Deepak Singh were working for a foreign-based gangster, with a second alleged plot against a Delhi businessman in an extortion case.
articles.image_caption: Delhi Police Special Cell officers pose with the two arrested men, their faces covered, after the arrests in Delhi and Mumbai. Police say the men were tasked by a foreign-based gangster with attacking a Bollywood actor and a Delhi businessman.
articles.nri_angle: Gang threats against Bollywood figures have repeatedly made headlines for diaspora audiences; police say this plot, allegedly run by a foreign-based gangster, was stopped before any attack took place.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Faulty Router in Copper-to-Fibre Upgrade Caused FAA Ground Stop, Duffy Says
articles.excerpt: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a router changed during L3Harris's routine maintenance flooded the air traffic network, and that more than 20,000 flights have been disrupted since Friday.
articles.nri_angle: The ground stop snarled US departures nationwide, including Air India and other India-bound services used heavily by the diaspora; schedules are expected to normalise by the end of Sunday.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bengaluru Pink Line Opens to Crowds, Roses and Doubts Over Partial Route
articles.excerpt: The 7.5-km Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere stretch cut a 20-to-30-minute road trip to about 10 minutes on day one, but commuters say the unfinished underground section still leaves cross-city journeys fragmented.
articles.image_caption: A Bengaluru Metro Pink Line train on an elevated section of the line. The 7.5-km Kalena Agrahara–Suddagunte Palya (Tavarekere) stretch opened to passengers on Saturday, a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated it.
articles.nri_angle: Bannerghatta Road is home to many of Bengaluru's technology workers, including returning NRIs, for whom the corridor's commute has been a daily cost of living in the city.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Rules Out Cyberattack as FAA Ground Stop Probe Points to Overloaded Aging Network
articles.excerpt: The nationwide ground stop was lifted at 8:15 p.m. ET Friday after more than four hours. FlightAware counted 5,117 US cancellations on Friday; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed routers overloaded on a legacy system.
articles.image_caption: The Federal Aviation Administration headquarters in Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: Indian travellers connecting through US hubs were among the estimated 1.5 million passengers stranded; Air India had already warned of US delays from the ground stop.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: FAA lifted ground stop at 8:15 p.m. ET

articles.title: IAF Helicopter in PM Modi's Convoy Grounded in Mysuru After Technical Snag
articles.excerpt: One of three helicopters in the Prime Minister's convoy could not take off from the Jayachamaraja Wadiyar helipad after his Mysuru programme. Modi continued in another aircraft; technicians are repairing the grounded helicopter.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Four Earthquakes Shake Jammu and Kashmir in 12 Hours, No Damage Reported
articles.excerpt: Tremors of magnitude 2.7 to 3.9 were recorded in the Doda-Kishtwar belt and in Leh on Saturday, at depths of 5 to 15 kilometres. Officials reported no loss of life or damage to property.
articles.nri_angle: Families abroad with relatives in the Chenab Valley can note the official position: all four tremors were minor and no damage was reported anywhere in the Union Territory.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi Calls Political Opponents 'Fascists' at Bharat Summit in Hyderabad
articles.excerpt: Addressing the valedictory session of the Bharat Summit 2026, the Leader of the Opposition said fascists 'jump out of the woodwork when systems collapse' and launched a social security scheme for Telangana gig workers.
articles.nri_angle: The Hyderabad summit drew delegates from around 70 countries, and the political row around it reached diaspora audiences following Indian politics abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Clears 26 New Border Roads in Arunachal, The Hindu Reports
articles.excerpt: The Cabinet Committee on Security reportedly cleared ICBR-III along the LAC earlier this year, with 33 ITBP bridges sanctioned since September, even as Eastern Sector talks and face-offs continue side by side.

sources.label: Chetan Bharat Current Affairs (summarising The Hindu)

articles.nri_angle: Border infrastructure in Arunachal shapes India-China stability, a long-running concern for diaspora readers following India's security posture; no direct reader action applies.

articles.title: Delhi Ministers Order Half Their Staff Home as Air Stays Very Poor
articles.excerpt: Delhi's overall AQI was 348 on Saturday morning, down from Friday's 24-hour average of 373 and Friday morning's reported 494 peak, as two ministers applied a 50 per cent work-from-home cap in their departments.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families with relatives in Delhi and travellers heading to the capital, the attendance caps and a forecast of further deterioration signal that the disruption will continue into the coming days.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items: Overall AQI touched 494 at 7:31 a.m. on November 13.

articles.title: Rs 1 Lakh Crore for Research, but PhD Scholars Wait Months for Their Stipends
articles.excerpt: An India Today feature asks why young scientists are struggling while a Rs 1 lakh crore research corpus rolls out — as fellowship holders report months without pay and a poll finds a quarter of scholars netting under Rs 10,000 a month.
articles.image_caption: An editorial illustration shows a vault of research funds feeding a pipe wrapped in red tape, with scholars collecting a trickle of coins below. India has a Rs 1 lakh crore research and innovation corpus, while many PhD fellows report stipend delays of months.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian researchers abroad weighing a return, and for diaspora families funding PhD students in India, the gap between headline research money and on-time stipends shapes whether talent stays, leaves, or comes back.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: U-19 Cricketer Nandini, 17, Dies by Suicide in Telangana; Family Alleges Harassment
articles.excerpt: The Vikarabad teenager had recently been selected for a BCCI Under-19 team, according to reports. Her family has accused two men of harassing her, and police have registered a case of suspicious death.
articles.nri_angle: A 17-year-old cricketer's death in Telangana, soon after a BCCI Under-19 selection, raises questions Indian families everywhere ask about the safety and support of young women in sport.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kochi to Set Up Seven Air Quality Monitors as Pollution Concern Mounts
articles.excerpt: Kochi Corporation plans seven new monitoring stations for Rs 10 lakh as two of the pollution board's three continuous stations have been down for over six months, leaving only Eloor operational.
articles.image_caption: A motorcyclist wearing a mask rides through haze past a construction site. Kochi Corporation plans seven new air quality monitoring stations as concern mounts over the city's pollution levels.
articles.nri_angle: Kochi's air and its broken monitors matter to the large Kerala diaspora with family in the city, who rely on local AQI data to judge conditions at home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mirwaiz Returns to Jama Masjid After Two Weeks of House Detention, Backs 10 PM Wazwan Deadline
articles.excerpt: In his first Friday sermon since the restrictions began, Mirwaiz Umar Farooq criticised curbs on his religious work and welcomed the Kashmir Waza Association's move to end wedding dinners by 10 p.m.
articles.nri_angle: Developments around Kashmir's chief cleric and Jama Masjid are closely followed by the Kashmiri diaspora; the wedding-feast reform also speaks to community celebrations abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Wants Positive Ties With Bangladesh, Says MEA Amid Hasina Extradition Row
articles.excerpt: New Delhi calls Hasina's extradition a legal matter, postpones the November 17-18 consular dialogue in Dhaka, and says other channels on trade, water and borders remain open.
articles.nri_angle: India-Bangladesh consular cooperation on visas, travel documents and repatriation directly affects diaspora families with ties on both sides of the border.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: WHO Classifies El Niño Health Impacts Emergency, Flags India High Risk
articles.excerpt: WHO's September assessment lists high or very high risks for India from heat, dengue and leptospirosis, with malaria in parts of the northeast, as the WMO says El Niño is expected to reach record strength by December.

sources.label: World Health Organization — Global Public Health Situation Analysis, El Niño 2026

articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers with family in India, WHO's assessment names the specific risks to watch by region — heat, dengue and leptospirosis nationally, and malaria in parts of the northeast — and the household precautions that follow from them.

articles.title: Man Dies After Biting Explosive Handed to Him as Rasgulla Sweet
articles.excerpt: Police in Madhya Pradesh's Dindori district say a 35-year-old man died after a crude boar-hunting explosive, described to him as a rasgulla, detonated in his mouth, and two men have been held as officers probe whether it was killing or mischief.
articles.nri_angle: A widely shared India news story with no direct action for diaspora readers; its relevance is the police investigation into crude hunting explosives circulating as ordinary food.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items: Charges: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
